messages.author: 9e35739f18a45ee9
messages.subject: big data in mirt
parts:
Hi all, I'm trying to run a 3-factor mirt() on 10,000 polytomous items (3 categories each, graded) in Windows (no missing data; method="EM").  Obviously it's taking a very long time, so I was wondering if you have any suggestions for how to decrease that computation time.  I have many compute cores available and noticed there is a mirtCluster() function in mirt, but I've found things are often more complicated in Windows.  Any suggestions?  If all I need to do is take advantage of the mirtCluster() function, would you mind posting an example of how I'd use it for this problem?

Thanks so much!

Tyler

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: big data in mirt
parts:
mirtCluster() has an OpenMP option to allow for that type of multi-threading, though on Windows this won't be of much use. Might be better to run your analyses on a *unix distribution with this option as then at least the E-step could be computed more quickly. 

Phil
